ArraySamplingOptions.description: Sample all entries of the observed fields, concatenated in the order of ``fields``.
ArraySamplingOptions.title: ArraySamplingOptions

CheckpointsTruthOptions.description:
Generate the data from the checkpoints of an earlier run of the forward solver.

The solver reads the true states at the measurement times from the checkpoints at
``path``; it needs :class:`kipe.forward_solver.SupportsCheckpoints`. The run may differ
from the model of the ``forward_solver`` section (e.g., in its time step or parameters), as
long as the solver can read its checkpoints into the model's state.

path.description:
Location of the checkpoints, as the solver understands it (e.g., the output directory of
the run).
path.title: Path

CheckpointsTruthOptions.title: CheckpointsTruthOptions

DifferenceModelOptions.description: Measured data are the sampled fields; innovation = measured - predicted.
DifferenceModelOptions.title: DifferenceModelOptions

EstimationOptions.description: Parameter estimation with the reduced-order unscented Kalman filter (ROUKF).

sigma_points.description:
Sigma-point stencil, the pattern along which the estimates are perturbed. Each sigma
point costs one forward run per measurement time:

- ``simplex``: :math:`p + 1` sigma points, the cheapest.
- ``canonical``: :math:`2p` sigma points, :math:`\pm` along each parameter.
- ``unique``: one sigma point at the estimate, no spread: no correction. A sanity check
  of the whole pipeline (with the true parameters, the innovations are pure noise).

iterations.description:
Number of passes over the measurements. Each pass after the first starts from the
previous estimate, with the initial uncertainty.
iterations.title: Iterations

EstimationOptions.title: EstimationOptions

ForwardSolverOptions.description:
How to construct the forward solver.

kipe imports ``factory`` and calls it with ``arguments`` as keyword arguments. The factory
can be a class or a function; it must return an object that conforms to
:class:`kipe.forward_solver.ForwardSolver`.

factory.description:
Import path of the factory, ``"module:name"``, e.g.,
``"kipe.examples.fitzhugh_nagumo:Solver"``.
factory.title: Factory

arguments.description: Keyword arguments passed to the factory, as given (no path resolution).
arguments.title: Arguments

ForwardSolverOptions.title: ForwardSolverOptions

MeasurementOptions.description: One measurement: which fields it observes, its data, and how to compare them.

data.description: Where the measured data are: read by ``estimation``, written by ``synthesis``.

times.description:
Measurement times: a list or a range. Required by ``synthesis`` (the times to
generate); for ``estimation`` a selection from the times in the data, all if not
given.
times.title: Times

spatial_sampling.description:
How the observed fields are brought to the measurement locations; the kind is selected
by ``type``, ``array`` by default.

model.description: How predicted data are computed from the sampled fields and compared with the data.

MeasurementOptions.title: MeasurementOptions

MeshSamplingOptions.description:
Interpolate the observed field onto a measurement mesh (FEniCSx backend).

The field must be a distributed field whose function space the forward solver provides
(:class:`kipe.fenicsx.forward_solver.SupportsFunctionSpaces`). The measurement mesh need
not match the solver's mesh. The data are in the order of the mesh file: by vertex for
``P1``, by cell for ``DG0``, independent of the number of ranks; for a vector field without
projection, the components of each vertex or cell one after another.

mesh.description: Path to the measurement mesh, an XDMF file.
mesh.title: Mesh

mesh_name.description:
Name of the mesh in the XDMF file (its grid): ``mesh`` as dolfinx writes it; meshio
writes ``Grid``.
mesh_name.title: Mesh Name

element.description:
Finite element on the measurement mesh: vertex values (``P1``) or cell values
(``DG0``).
element.title: Element

projection.description:
What is measured of a vector field; all components if not given. A direction, e.g.,
``[0, 0, 1]`` for the z component (normalized by kipe), or ``surface_normal``: the
component along the cell normal of a surface mesh (needs ``element: DG0``, one normal per
cell). The normal's orientation follows the order of each cell's vertices in the mesh file,
as ``ufl.CellNormal``: the right-hand rule for triangles in 3D, the tangent rotated by +90°
for lines in 2D; it is outward only if the mesh's cells are oriented that way.
projection.title: Projection

padding.description:
Distance, in mesh units, by which a measurement point may lie outside the solver's mesh,
e.g., where a surface mesh cuts slightly across the solver's boundary. Such a point takes
the value of the field in the nearest cell, extrapolated; a point farther out is an
error.
padding.title: Padding

MeshSamplingOptions.title: MeshSamplingOptions

NoiseOptions.description:
Measurement noise: assumed by ``estimation``, added by ``synthesis``.

``synthesis.noise`` can set another noise for synthesis to add, e.g., none.

stddev.description: Standard deviation of the noise, in the unit of the data.
stddev.title: Stddev

seed.description:
Seed of the noise added by ``synthesis`` (required there, unless it adds none, see
``synthesis.noise``). The noise of the k-th time of the measurement is drawn from
``numpy.random.default_rng([seed, k])``, so it does not depend on the other times.
Measurements must have different seeds.
seed.title: Seed

NoiseOptions.title: NoiseOptions

NumpyDataOptions.description:
Measurement data in a numpy ``.npz`` file.

The file holds the arrays ``times``, shape ``(n,)``, and ``values``, shape ``(n, m)``: m
values at each of the n times.

path.description:
Path to the ``.npz`` file. With several noise realizations
(``synthesis.realizations``), it contains the placeholder ``{realization}``, e.g.,
``"data/r{realization}/u.npz"`` or ``"data/u_{realization:02d}.npz"``: each realization has
its own file. In quotes, since YAML reads braces in ``{type: ..., path: ...}`` as a
mapping.
path.title: Path

NumpyDataOptions.title: NumpyDataOptions

OutputOptions.description: Where and how kipe writes its results.

path.description: Directory for all results. Subcommands write into subdirectories.
path.title: Path

log_level.description: Minimum level of the log messages kipe writes.
log_level.title: Log Level

OutputOptions.title: OutputOptions

ParameterPrior.description:
Initial estimate of one estimated parameter and its uncertainty.

The two define the prior (Gaussian in the estimated parameter :math:`\theta`) and the
starting state of the filter: the standard deviation sets the initial size of the
sigma-point stencil used for the derivative-free linearization, and the initial weight
against the measurement noise.

``log`` and ``multiplicative`` take a ``relative_stddev``, ``additive`` an absolute
``stddev``.

initial.description:
Initial estimate (prior mean), as physical value. The solver's nominal value if not
given.
initial.title: Initial

relative_stddev.description:
Standard deviation relative to ``initial``, e.g., ``0.3`` for 30%. For ``log`` and
``multiplicative``.

Converted to the standard deviation of :math:`\theta`, to first order around ``initial``:
:math:`\sigma_\theta` = ``relative_stddev`` / ln 2 for ``log``, :math:`\sigma_\theta` =
``relative_stddev`` for ``multiplicative``. So both give the same prior as long as
``relative_stddev`` is small. For large values they differ: ``log`` keeps the sign of the
parameter, at the price of an asymmetric distribution. ``kipe list-parameters`` shows the
resulting 1σ range.
relative_stddev.title: Relative Stddev

stddev.description: Absolute standard deviation, in the parameter's physical unit. For ``additive``.
stddev.title: Stddev

reparameterization.description: Overrides the section's ``reparameterization`` for this parameter.

ParameterPrior.title: ParameterPrior

ParametersOptions.description:
Selection, initial estimate and reparameterization of the estimated parameters.

``kipe list-parameters`` shows the names the forward solver accepts.

reparameterization.description:
How the estimated parameter :math:`\theta` relates to the physical value :math:`\phi`,
relative to the initial estimate :math:`\phi_0`. Default for all parameters in
``select``, each can override it.

Available reparameterizations:

- ``log``: :math:`\phi = \phi_0 2^\theta`, starting at :math:`\theta = 0`, with a
  ``relative_stddev``. Keeps the sign of :math:`\phi_0`; the initial estimate may be
  positive or negative, but not zero.
- ``multiplicative``: :math:`\phi = \phi_0 \theta`, starting at :math:`\theta = 1`, with
  a ``relative_stddev``. The initial estimate must not be zero; :math:`\phi` can change
  sign.
- ``additive``: :math:`\phi = \phi_0 + \theta`, starting at :math:`\theta = 0`, with an
  absolute ``stddev``. :math:`\theta` is the deviation from the initial estimate, in the
  parameter's physical unit. Accepts any initial estimate, including zero.

select.description:
Estimated parameters: parameter name -> initial estimate and uncertainty. All other
parameters keep their nominal values.
select.title: Select

ParametersOptions.title: ParametersOptions

PointSamplingOptions.description:
Evaluate the observed field at given points (FEniCSx backend).

The field must be a distributed field whose function space the forward solver provides
(:class:`kipe.fenicsx.forward_solver.SupportsFunctionSpaces`). The data are in the order of
``points``; for a vector field, the components of each point one after another.

points.description:
Coordinates of the measurement points, one list per point, e.g., ``[[0.5, 0.5], [0.2,
0.8]]`` in 2D. Each point must lie in the solver's mesh.
points.title: Points

PointSamplingOptions.title: PointSamplingOptions

RunTruthOptions.description: Generate the data by running the forward solver with its nominal parameters.
RunTruthOptions.title: RunTruthOptions

SynthesisNoiseOptions.description: Noise that synthesis adds to the data of a measurement.

stddev.description: Standard deviation of the noise, in the unit of the data; 0 for noise-free data.
stddev.title: Stddev

SynthesisNoiseOptions.title: SynthesisNoiseOptions

truth.description:
Source of the true state the data are generated from: a run of the forward solver, or
its checkpoints.

noise.description:
Noise synthesis adds to the data of the listed measurements (measurement name ->
noise), instead of their ``noise.stddev``, which estimation assumes: for noise-free data
(``stddev: 0``) or studies with misspecified noise. Measurements not listed get their
``noise.stddev``.
noise.title: Noise

realizations.description:
Number of noise realizations, e.g., for the statistics of the estimates over the noise.
Synthesis computes the true state once and writes the data of realizations
:math:`r = 0, \dots, n - 1`, each to the ``data.path`` of the measurements with
``{realization}`` replaced by :math:`r`; ``kipe estimation --realization r`` estimates from
one of them. Realization 0 has the noise of a study without realizations.
realizations.title: Realizations

TimeRange.description: Equidistant times from ``start`` to ``stop``, both included.
TimeRange.title: TimeRange
